preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 1000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 200000 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2e5) representing the number of vertices.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and a[0] == 1 and all(1 <= x <= n for x in a) and len(set(a)) == n for a, n in zip([list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]], [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains n integers a₁, a₂, ..., aₙ (1 ≤ aᵢ ≤ n; aᵢ ≠ aⱼ; a₁ = 1) representing the BFS visiting order, with all vertices appearing exactly once.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == str(min_height) for i, (n, a) in enumerate(zip([int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]])) if (min_height := max(0, max(1 + a.index(x) - a.index(a[0]) for x in a if x != a[0]))))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the minimum possible height of a tree with the given BFS visiting order a. The height is computed as the maximum depth of any vertex, where the depth of vertex a[i] is 1 + the number of vertices before it in the BFS order that are its ancestors.
